about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Sarah McBride

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RESTORE BACK BAY STUDY
statements.title: RESTORE BACK BAY STUDY
sentences: For the last 6 years as the President pro-tempore of the State senate, Dave led a caucus that raised the minimum wage, passed paid family and medical leave, advanced historic gun safety legislation, and protected vulnerable neighborhoods whose rights and freedoms have been anything but secure.
During my time in the Delaware General Assembly, Deb and I teamed up often, including to lead the successful effort to pass paid family and medical leave statewide.
I thank my former colleagues and my friends in Leg Hall for their years of service to the greatest State in the history of the Union, and best wishes to a happy retirement. ____________________
I will keep working to restore the Back Bay study because Delawareans cannot afford for this study to simply be abandoned.
I had the chance to see their devotion to their constituents, and I will take a moment in this Chamber to celebrate their service.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICA IS GREAT BECAUSE AMERICA CAN CHANGE
statements.title: AMERICA IS GREAT BECAUSE AMERICA CAN CHANGE
sentences: Mr. Speaker, last week, I had the privilege of visiting a historic landmark in Delaware formerly known as the Hockessin Colored School, which stands as a physical reminder of both the sin of segregation that scars our history and the change that is possible when dedicated citizens dare to build a more perfect Union, one that lives up to our values and our promise.

Now, one of three sites in Delaware that are part of the Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park, it tells the story of Sarah Bulah, whose daughter would watch the bus pass her by on its way to an all-White school and who dared to fight to end legal discrimination in education for her daughter and all students.

In 1952, the first Black attorney barred in Delaware, Louis Redding, represented the Bulah family in court, securing a win at the State level that would ultimately be appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court, consolidated alongside four other cases into Brown v. Board of Education.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FACING AN INFLECTION POINT IN THIS NATION AND THE WORLD
statements.title: FACING AN INFLECTION POINT IN THIS NATION AND THE WORLD
sentences: In cities across our country, masked paramilitary agents are brutally murdering American citizens, disappearing immigrants without due process, and acting with cheered-on cruelty that mirrors a secret police force.
Do we destroy our Union, our Constitution, and our democracy, or do we choose to build a more perfect Union?
They want to destroy jobs and the American worker by unleashing unregulated technology that leaves the rich richer and everyone else behind.
While real disagreements exist and while our politics and this place don't always bring out the best in us, I see every day back in Delaware that we are not as divided as the algorithms make it seem.
We can be truly profamily by building a cradle-through-career support system with paid leave, universal childcare, and strong public schools so that it is actually affordable to start a family.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DELAWARE DAY
statements.title: DELAWARE DAY
sentences: On that momentous day in 1787, the greatest State in the Union became the first State in the Union, boldly seizing the mantle of leadership by ratifying the United States Constitution before any of our hesitant sister States dared to do so.

With more than 25 years in nonprofit service as an attorney, advocate, and administrator, Sue has devoted her life to advancing justice for people who are too often overlooked: survivors of violence, impoverished families, refugees, and those experiencing homelessness.
Tariffs are driving up grocery prices even higher and contributing to price uncertainty.

That is why I am proud to be a sponsor of legislation that would restore some common sense by banning the President from imposing tariffs without congressional approval, capping the cost of childcare, expanding health coverage, creating new pathways to homeownership, raising the minimum wage, and expanding tax deductions for working-class people.

Mr. Speaker, after Thanksgiving season, where so many families felt the strain, the message from Delaware is clear: We need solutions, not tariffs and cuts to healthcare but policies that make life more affordable. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3838, STREAMLINING PROCUREMENT FOR EFFECTIVE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY AND NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026;
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3838, STREAMLINING PROCUREMENT FOR EFFECTIVE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY AND NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026; AND PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION...
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I know a few Members of this Chamber can't seem to muster any maturity when they have a transgender colleague, but members of the U.S. Armed Forces can and have.
For years, transgender people have been serving in our military.
There was no problem until Donald Trump decided to fire thousands of qualified, capable servicemembers simply because of their gender identity.
My second amendment restores retirement benefits to transgender veterans who were forced out of the Armed Forces just shy of 20 years of service.
Many received approval only to have it revoked simply because of their gender identity.
That is why I introduced an amendment to repeal this ban because this ban doesn't strengthen our military.

Unfortunately, the majority in this body refuses to let us vote on these amendments, but I will not stop standing up for every patriot who serves our country, which until now I thought was a noncontroversial and bipartisan idea.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRANSGENDER AMERICANS SERVE WITH HONOR
statements.title: TRANSGENDER AMERICANS SERVE WITH HONOR
sentences: They are brave, honorable, and committed patriots who have also dared to have the courage to say out loud that they are transgender.
We see every single day what honor, discipline, and sacrifice looks like regardless of someone's gender identity.

These individuals met the same rigorous standards as their peers, the same physical exams, screenings, and background checks; and in many cases, under intense scrutiny, they didn't just meet those standards, they exceeded them.

In a recent hearing, the Secretary of Defense even commended these patriots, only to frantically retract his praise when he decided that their being transgender, one small part of who these soldiers are, somehow outweighed their years of proven high performance and service to this country.
Across Delaware, from Georgetown to Wilmington, I have met transgender veterans who served this Nation with distinction.
I salute every transgender servicemember.
Mr. Speaker, I reject that message.
I will not stop fighting for a country that is truly worthy of their service. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EQUAL OPPORTUNITY FOR ALL INVESTORS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: EQUAL OPPORTUNITY FOR ALL INVESTORS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Current law allows only millionaires to invest in the markets that fuel small businesses, shutting out countless Americans, especially women, veterans, and people of color, based on wealth, not knowledge.
I urge all my colleagues to vote in favor of this commonsense, bipartisan legislation today.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THANKING OFFICER ROBERT SCISCO
statements.title: THANKING OFFICER ROBERT SCISCO
sentences: I will not stop fighting until we restore this funding so that no one in Delaware goes hungry. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to this big, ugly bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WILMINGTON POLICE ATHLETIC LEAGUE
statements.title: WILMINGTON POLICE ATHLETIC LEAGUE
sentences: Mr. Speaker, last week I had the privilege of visiting the Wilmington Police Athletic League, a place where community and opportunity are shaping the next generation of Delawareans.
I am proud to stand with them, and I will keep working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to expand the resources that make their mission possible. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: KEEP RURAL HOSPITALS OPEN AS LIFELINE
statements.title: KEEP RURAL HOSPITALS OPEN AS LIFELINE
sentences: When Medicaid is gutted, rural hospitals don't just struggle.
They rely on Medicaid to keep the lights on and the doors open.
Take that funding away, and entire regions lose access to maternity care, cancer treatment, mental health services, and more.
Before Medicaid expansion, clinics were closing, nurses were being laid off, and people were driving for hours just to see a doctor.
This budget would impose endless red tape and import the worst parts of the private healthcare system, confusing paperwork and needless bureaucracy, into the Medicaid program.
In Delaware, that will mean 40,000 of our neighbors--working families, children, seniors in assisted living, and people managing chronic conditions--getting dropped from coverage.

It means working people in Delaware will skip doctors' appointments because they have lost their insurance, only to end up in the emergency room and facing longer wait times and crushing medical bills.
Rural hospitals are left to absorb the costs while patients are burdened with life-altering debt, and, yes, it means more preventable deaths.
All of this, Mr. Speaker, is just to partially--just partially--pay for tax breaks for billionaires.
Their facilities serve hundreds and, in some cases, thousands of Medicaid patients.
Cuts to Medicaid aren't just cuts to line items on a budget.

Mr. Speaker, let's be honest about what this is: a budget that raises costs for working families, adds red tape for patients and providers, and gives handouts to billionaires, all while risking the collapse of rural healthcare systems.
Mr. Speaker, I will tell you what that means in real life.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: They want to eviscerate healthcare so long as they get tax breaks for their billionaire best friends.
It is not too late to protect Medicaid.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING AMERICAN MARITIME RESEARCH
statements.title: PROTECTING AMERICAN MARITIME RESEARCH
sentences: More than 1.6 million veterans rely on Medicaid for their health coverage.
My constituents are warning me, and they are right, that cuts to SNAP, Medicaid, and VA services will fall hardest on disabled and aging veterans, especially in rural areas and communities of color.
House Republicans have chosen to unilaterally pursue a budget that puts tax cuts for billionaires ahead of care for the people who wore the uniform.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of the ANCHOR Act, a bipartisan bill to protect American maritime research and strengthen our national security.

That is why I am proud to cosponsor the ANCHOR Act, which directs the National Science Foundation to develop a plan to upgrade cybersecurity and communications across the U.S. academic research fleet, including the Sharp.
The ANCHOR Act passed out of committee with bipartisan support, and I urge my colleagues to vote to get it over the finish line.
Mr. Speaker, let me be clear: We don't support veterans by handing them a folded flag with one hand and cutting their lifelines with the other.
This Memorial Day, I urge my colleagues to follow the famous charge of President Lincoln.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
statements.title: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
sentences: Her daughter relies on Medicaid to pay for the formula that keeps her alive.

As her mother wrote plainly to me: ``If she loses Medicaid, she will die.'' Mr. Speaker, we must not gut Medicaid to give tax breaks to billionaires while moms are begging for their children to survive.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues: Protect Medicaid and protect this child.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NEARLY ONE IN FOUR DELAWAREANS RELY ON MEDICAID
statements.title: NEARLY ONE IN FOUR DELAWAREANS RELY ON MEDICAID
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today as the Representative of the nearly one in four Delawareans who rely on Medicaid: families, children, seniors, and people with disabilities whose lives now hang in the balance.
Republicans in Congress have proposed not only the largest cut in Medicaid in American history but the single largest evisceration of healthcare in American history, period.
Without Medicaid, she told me that she could die.

They all agree: Republican cuts to Medicaid will do irreparable harm, eliminating a lifeline for their patients, and putting further strain on our hospital systems that are already facing a workforce crisis.

If that weren't enough, the bill also includes what can only be described as a backdoor abortion ban, prohibiting Medicaid funding from going to family planning clinics that provide abortion services, even if that funding isn't being used for abortion care.
This means shuttering access to trusted providers and family planning clinics, especially in rural areas where options are already scarce.
They are doing all of this while forcing working families to pay more out of pocket.
Republicans in Congress want to tax the healthcare of working people all to just partially pay for tax cuts for the wealthy.
Let's review what their budget will actually do: It raises costs for working families across the country through new out-of-pocket expenses, higher premiums, and loss in coverage.
It adds $3.7 trillion to the deficit, not to expand care or invest in working people, but to fund tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans.
Mr. Speaker, I am going to end with the words of another Delawarean, a single mom: ``Without Medicaid, neither of us would have health insurance.
If we lose Medicaid, we lose everything.'' She added this: ``P.S., I am a healthcare worker with a bachelor's degree.
I urge my colleagues to reject this cruel and catastrophic proposal. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: UNITED STATES POSTAL SERVICE IS NOT JUST A CONVENIENCE
statements.title: UNITED STATES POSTAL SERVICE IS NOT JUST A CONVENIENCE
sentences: This administration's effort to privatize the Postal Service would mean higher costs, slower service, and the elimination of rural delivery because corporations won't serve what isn't profitable.

Yet, this administration and House Republicans are advancing a proposal to shrink the retirement benefits for Federal employees who are retiring before 62, all to help pay for tax cuts for the wealthy.

Congratulating Students of Charter School of Wilmington Mr. Speaker, I rise to celebrate an extraordinary achievement by students from the Charter School of Wilmington, who were just named national winners of Samsung's Solve for Tomorrow STEM competition.
While I am a proud graduate of Cab Calloway, I couldn't help but come to the well of the House to congratulate the Charter School of Wilmington.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CUTTING LIFELINE OF INSTITUTE OF MUSEUM AND LIBRARY SERVICES
statements.title: CUTTING LIFELINE OF INSTITUTE OF MUSEUM AND LIBRARY SERVICES
sentences: In Dover, librarians are helping my neighbors navigate Social Security delays.
Mr. Speaker, I urge the administration to reverse course, and I stand with my colleagues in demanding full funding for the services our communities need and deserve. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOOD BANKS FACING URGENT CRISIS
statements.title: FOOD BANKS FACING URGENT CRISIS
sentences: I am proud to stand with them in this effort, and I look forward to seeing Seaford become a symbol of progress and opportunities for generations to come. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COMMUNITY LEGAL AID SOCIETY OF DELAWARE
statements.title: COMMUNITY LEGAL AID SOCIETY OF DELAWARE
sentences: For many of our most vulnerable residents, including individuals with disabilities, survivors of domestic violence, and low-income families, CLASI has been a beacon of hope and a lifeline in pursuit of safe, quality, and affordable housing.
I will continue to fight to restore these funds.

I will fight for the future of CLASI and other fair housing programs, and I will fight to ensure that every person in Delaware and across the country can rent or buy a safe, quality, and affordable home.
The Delawareans' lives touched by CLASI's work should know that I stand with them.
Together, we will continue the work of guaranteeing fair housing for all.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING AGRICULTURE, THE BACKBONE OF DELAWARE'S ECONOMY
statements.title: PROTECTING AGRICULTURE, THE BACKBONE OF DELAWARE'S ECONOMY
sentences: Mr. Speaker, last week, when the House was out of session and I was in the greatest State in the Union, Delaware, I met with a family farmer in Sussex County who continues to farm the same land that her family has farmed for more than a century.
I will stand here in opposition to any executive or legislative action that puts our farmers at risk because when we fail farmers, we fail all Americans. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DELIVERING FOR DELAWAREANS
statements.title: DELIVERING FOR DELAWAREANS
sentences: The attacks we have seen in recent days on public servants and lifesaving programs administered by USAID don't just put our security and health globally at risk, they lay the foundation here at home to gut Federal support for education, for healthcare, for housing, for childcare, and for workers.
If they can do what they are doing at USAID, then they can do it anywhere in the Federal Government.
We shouldn't pretend that this path doesn't ultimately lead to Social Security and Medicare.
